title: Reservation probation window and elastic buffering protocol for Dedicated capacity
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Define and implement a provisioning workflow that uses a probation window and an elastic buffer credit system to reduce risk for both customers and Redwood when committing Dedicated capacity. The flow should allow tentative reservations (probation), automated simulation of expected throughput, a short guaranteed window with elastic buffer credits, and clear decommit / scale-down rules to avoid unexpected overcommit.
background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity often want throughput guarantees but we see significant variance in actual utilization during initial ramp. Current reservation commitments are binary (commit or not) and lead to either overprovisioning or disappointed expectations. We need a staged contract pattern that lets customers get initial guarantees while Redwood gathers real workload signals and preserves operational flexibility.
goals: Reduce provisioning friction for customers who need guarantees but cannot accurately forecast first-week traffic
Protect Redwood fleet economics by bounding initial committed liability
Provide clear UX and contract language around probation, credits, and decommit rules
Make autoscaling policies and fleet controls compatible with probation windows and buffer credits
non_goals: Replace long-term reservation contracts (annual committed throughput),
Complex per-tenant custom SLAs beyond templated probation options
proposal: Introduce a three-stage reservation lifecycle: 1) Tentative reservation: customer requests capacity and selects a probation profile (7/14/30 day). No hard billing commitment; a refundable deposit/credit holds the slot. 2) Probation window: Redwood provisions capacity with a soft guarantee up to X% of requested throughput. System collects traffic metrics, runs simulated load tests (based on sample prompts / inferred seq lengths), and proposes final commit terms. 3) Commitment with Elastic Buffer: After probation, customer accepts a final reserved capacity with an attached elastic buffer credit pool (e.g., 10-30% burst credits) that can be used for short peaks. Buffer consumption beyond the pool is billed at overage rates or triggers autoscale fallback rules. Include a graceful decommit policy for lower-than-expected actuals (automatic scale-down with 30-day notice or credit refund ramp).
api_and_console_changes: Reservation API: new fields probation_profile, deposit_token, buffer_credit_amount, probation_metrics_url
Console: reservation wizard step for selecting probation window and buffer size; visual simulation results (expected p95 latency, cost delta)
Hooks for autoscaling policies to annotate nodes as probation-bound (affects eviction and preemption rules)
acceptance_criteria: Customers can create tentative reservations with probation_profile via API and Console
Probation metrics are generated and viewable within 24 hours of provisioning
A new buffer_credit accounting exists in billing and is displayed in Console usage breakdowns
Autoscaling policies treat probation-bound nodes according to the documented fallback rules
SLA calculator updated to show effective guarantee during probation vs post-commit
metrics: % of reservations that convert from tentative->commit within probation window
Average variance between requested throughput and actual utilization in first 30 days
Buffer credit burn-rate and % of customers hitting buffer ceiling
Number of scale-down events triggered by probation decommit policy
Revenue impact: delta between current booking vs projected under probation model
dependencies: DES-2219 (reservation wizard UI for probation selection)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers abuse buffer credits to avoid committing. Mitigation: limit buffer to short windows (max 72 hours sustained) and tiered overage pricing.
Risk: Complexity in fleet scheduling leads to degraded utilization. Mitigation: run a staging simulation phase and conservative defaults (small buffer, short probation) before enabling broadly.
Risk: Billing disputes around deposit/refunds. Mitigation: clear T&Cs and automatic refunding workflow instrumented in billing.
Risk: Engineering effort spikes for cross-team integration. Mitigation: phased rollout with pilot customers and feature flags.
open_questions: What is the right set of probation profiles to offer (7/14/30)?
How large should default buffer credits be relative to requested throughput (10%/20%/30%)?
Should deposit be mandatory for all tentative reservations or only > X throughput?
How do we model multi-region reservations with staggered probation windows?

rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal pilot with feature flag (small set of customers, conservative defaults). Phase 2: Beta to early-adopter accounts and SE-assisted onboarding. Phase 3: GA with documentation, updated SLA language, and billing automation. Backout plan: ability to revert tentative reservation creation and refund deposits, freeze new probation reservations if fleet instability detected.
